THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 -3-  NC: 2024:KHC:32704  MFA No. 8349 of 2016  C/W MFA No. 2828 of 2017 CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT
In both these appeals, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is questioned.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The undisputed facts is that, on 10.07.2014 at 7.00 p.m., while the petitioner was crossing the road in front of Dhanalaxmi Paints and Hardware at Hassan, car bearing Reg.No.KA-46/M-896 hit against him, due to which, he sustained injuries.

After taking treatment at Janapriya Hospital,
Hassan, the petitioner approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.15 lakhs.
Claim was opposed by the respondents.
After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal by impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.4,06,000/- with interest @ 9% p.a.

Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner is before this Court in NC:
2024:KHC:32704 M.F.A.No.2828/2017 whereas the Insurance Company assailing the quantum of compensation is before this Court in M.F.A.No.8349/2016.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.B.C.Seetharama Rao, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and Sri.B.Chethan, learned counsel for the petitioner.
5.
It is contended by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the petitioner has suffered fracture of left patella; he was under hospitalization for 6 days.

Medical evidence through PW-2/Dr.Abdul Basheer indicates limb disability of 30% whereas the Tribunal taken the whole body disability of 30% and assessed exorbitant compensation of Rs.2,34,000/- towards loss of future income.

The accident is of the year 2014 and the petitioner is entitled to just compensation for the injuries that he has sustained in the accident, the medical bills are manipulated, the petitioner is not operated with any implants, medical bills indicating the medicines prescribed for Hepatitis-B NC:
2024:KHC:32704 and other ailments are being billed, there is no reasonability in the medical bills of Rs.62,000/-.
Having regard to the inpatient bills to the tune of Rs.15,000/-, the proportionate medical expenses has to be reimbursed.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000/- towards future National Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri Kumaraswamy on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8714246/
3 prospects without any reason.

sentences.text:
For 6 days' inpatient, attendant charges is awarded at Rs.10,000/-,
which is excessive.
In the year 2014, no Banks will offer interest @ 9% per annum.
The Tribunal awarded interest without giving any cogent reasons and sought for modification.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the petitioner has suffered fracture of Patella and he is a businessman doing paint and hardware business, he is required to handle the painting work and the injuries certainly affect his earning capacity.
The Tribunal has not considered the future medical expenses and loss of income during laid-up.
If all these aspects are taken into NC: 2024:KHC:32704 consideration, compensation awarded is just and there is no need for reduction of compensation.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident and liability on the part of the respondent to pay compensation.
It is interesting to note that PW- 2/Dr.Abdul Basheer has assessed the limb disability at 30% whereas the Tribunal has accepted it as whole body disability.
The petitioner is doing paint and hardware business at Shanivarasanthe, a small village of Somavarapet and he being a small businessman, in what way the injuries affected him is not explained.
The Tribunal ignoring all these aspects assessed the limb disability as whole body disability though functional disability shall not exceed 5% in the facts and circumstances of the case.
In the year 2014, a person with no proof of income will earn not less than Rs.8,500/- per month.
The petitioner was aged 45 years at the time of accident and the applicable multiplier is '14'.

The petitioner is entitled for pain and suffering at Rs.40,000/-; medical expenses at Rs.25,000/-;
incidental expenses is restricted to Rs.5,000/-; loss of amenities and discomfort will be Rs.25,000/-; future medical expenses at Rs.10,000/-; loss of income for three months laid up is Rs.25,500/-.

Loss of income due to disability will be: Rs.8,500/-x12x14x5% = Rs.71,400/-, thereby the total compensation comes to Rs.2,01,900/- as against Rs.4,06,000/- assessed by the Tribunal,
thereby reducing the compensation by Rs.2,04,100/-.
It is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
10. As regarding rate of interest, the Tribunal has not assigned any special reasons to award 9% per annum,
Court is required to consider prevailing bank NC: 2024:KHC:32704 rate of interest.

In this regard, the Division Bench of this court in Ms.Joyeeta Bose and Ors. -vs- Venkateshan.V. and Ors. in M.F.A.No.5896/2018 c/w M.F.A.Nos.4444/2018 and 4659/2018 (MV) DD 24.08.2020 with reference to Section 149(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Rule 253 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Section 34 of Civil Procedure Code, at Para 52 has laid down principles regarding award of interest, it reads thus:
"52.

Thus, under Section 34 of CPC being squarely applicable to the interest awarded by the tribunal and Section 34 empowering the tribunal to award pendente lite National Insurance Co Ltd vs Sri Kumaraswamy on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8714246/
4 interest and discretion being vested with the Court/Tribunal to award interest from the date of suit or petition is to the maximum extent of 6% p.a. or in other words, not exceeding 6% p.a., the contention raised by the learned Advocates appearing for the Insurance Company deserves to be accepted and accordingly, it is accepted.
